text:
A Lake Wind Advisory is in effect, and Friday is a stay-inside-or-keep-it-short kind of day. Heavy rain and fog are already settled in, with more rain, occasional downpours, and a high near 63 ahead. South winds will run 15 to 22 mph, gusting as high as 40, so expect a raw, blustery feel even as temperatures rise. The lake will be rough, with waves around 5 to 7 feet at first, so this is not a boating day. Rain should taper to a chance of showers before 11 tonight as the wind swings northwest and temperatures drop toward 36.

Saturday brings the real reset, partly sunny but much colder, with a high near 44 and northwest gusts up to 33 mph. The models range from the low 40s to near 50, but every version keeps the wind in the plan, and a few showers remain possible. Keep Friday errands flexible, stay off the lake, and save Saturday outdoor time for a sheltered walk after the morning chill eases.

week.blurb: A wet, windy Friday peaks near 63, then showers taper after dark as colder air arrives.
A blustery Saturday brings sun and clouds, with a high near 44 and a chilly low around 32.
Sunday looks sunny and milder, reaching the mid 50s, with a cool, clear night ahead.
Monday stays sunny and mild, with a high near 60 and a comfortable setup for outdoor plans.
Tuesday looks mostly sunny and seasonably mild, reaching near 60 under light winds.
Wednesday brings mostly sunny skies and a high near 57, with a cooler feel by evening.
Thursday looks mostly sunny and mild, trending toward a high near 58.
